name: Nasal taping at night

lead: Nasal taping means wearing adhesive tape, commonly micropore paper tape or kinesiology tape, on the nose for hours or overnight to get a slimmer, more lifted or more defined nose. It is often marketed as a non-surgical mini nose job and spread on TikTok from the early 2020s.

Social-media users claim gradual cartilage remodelling, which is anecdotal. Plastic surgeons quoted in coverage say any change lasts only while the tape is worn, and the technique borrows from taping used after rhinoplasty to manage swelling. No clinical trials of cosmetic taping were located.

paras: Users apply strips across the bridge and sides of the nose before bed and remove them in the morning, repeating nightly. It is usually done as a free or low-cost add-on to a skincare routine.
Reported risks are skin irritation, contact dermatitis, breakouts and skin damage on removal, mainly in sensitive skin. Doctors quoted advise checking first if there are breathing problems.

lead: Nasal taping is a social-media technique in which people apply adhesive tape, commonly micropore paper tape or kinesiology tape, across the bridge and sides of the nose for several hours or overnight to get a slimmer, more lifted or more defined-looking nose. It is often marketed as a non-surgical mini nose job and is used by people who want a refined nose profile without surgery.[1]

Grokipedia reports that the trend grew on TikTok from the early 2020s and gained wide visibility in 2023 and 2024, and that plastic surgeons say taping cannot permanently reshape the nose, with any visible change lasting only while the tape is worn.[1] The technique borrows from taping and splinting used after rhinoplasty to manage swelling, where the nose is taped and splinted for about a week.[2]

Nose taping is separate from two related products with similar names. Nasal strips are drug-free adhesive strips with plastic splints that hold the nostrils open to widen the nasal passage, and mouth taping seals the lips during sleep to encourage nasal breathing.[3][4] No clinical trials of cosmetic nose taping were located.
infobox: Adhesive tape applied to the nose
Not a regulated device; tapes sold as general medical supplies

paras: Users typically clean and dry the nose and place one or more strips along the bridge and toward the nostrils, sometimes overlapping, then wear them for hours or overnight.[1] Tapes described as common choices are 3M-type paper micropore tape and elastic kinesiology tape, with hypoallergenic and breathable tapes preferred to limit irritation.[1]

Grokipedia traces the trend to TikTok tutorials from 2021, with growing visibility in late 2022 and 2023 and videos reaching tens of millions of views in 2024; it reports the related hashtag #facetape had nearly 730 million views by late 2023.[1] Post-rhinoplasty taping and splinting, in which the nose is taped and fitted with a splint that is removed about a week after surgery, predates the trend.[2]

Proponents claim reduced swelling, improved contour and better breathing during sleep. Plastic surgeons quoted in coverage say taping does not change bone or cartilage and cannot replace rhinoplasty; they describe it as more appropriate after surgery for swelling.[1] Nasal strips, unlike tape, are designed to widen the nasal passage and are the product intended for breathing.[1] Grokipedia is AI-generated and its reporting is treated here as secondary.

Nasal strips, sold since the 1990s under names such as Breathe Right, are adhesive bandages with plastic ribs that hold the nostrils open and are used during exercise, for congestion and for snoring; the only reported side effect is skin irritation from adhesive [3]. Wikipedia reports a study in which they increased nasal cavity volume in the front of the nose with airflow comparable to a decongestant spray [3].

Mouth taping, a separate 2020s social-media practice of sleeping with lips taped shut, was reported by Wikipedia to have very limited research as of 2023; two small studies in mild sleep apnea found lower apnea-hypopnea index and less snoring [4]. These practices concern breathing rather than nose shape.

Reported risks of taping skin include irritation, redness, contact dermatitis, breakouts, and skin damage on removal, particularly in people with sensitive skin or adhesive allergy.[1] Some commentary raises concern that repeated tension and removal could affect skin laxity, though this is not supported by published studies.[1] Medical professionals quoted advise consulting a doctor first, especially with underlying breathing problems.[1]

lore.intro: Nose taping is discussed mainly on short-video platforms as an overnight beauty hack; claims below are those described in coverage of the trend.[1]

claims.claim: Taping overnight slims or lifts the nose
Repeated taping gradually remodels the cartilage
Taping improves nasal breathing and sleep

timeline.event: Early TikTok tutorials adapt post-rhinoplasty taping for cosmetic use.[1]
Individual nose taping videos reach tens of millions of views.[1]
